::: {.callout-important}
## This lecture is a video lecture
There is no on-site lecture on 9 November 2026. The lecture is recorded as nine
short chapters (about 90 minutes in total) that you can watch in your own time.
Please watch them **before** you start the take-home examination on literature
reviews, which is published on Moodle on 9 November.
:::

## 🎯 Content and goals

The lecture uses the systematic literature review as the reference model and
shows what it means for the literature review section of your term paper or
thesis. After this session you can …

1. **choose** a type of review (narrative, integrative, scoping, systematic,
   meta-analysis, bibliometric) that fits a given purpose, and justify the
   choice;
2. **explain** what a literature review can establish and what it cannot;
3. **translate** a topic into a reviewable question and a concept table, and
   from there into a documented Boolean search string for Web of Science;
4. **assess** a search in terms of precision and recall, and validate it
   against known key publications;
5. **apply** explicit inclusion and exclusion criteria and document the
   selection in a PRISMA 2020 flow diagram;
6. **synthesise** literature with a concept matrix instead of summarising it
   paper by paper;
7. **identify** the main sources of bias in the literature, in your own search
   and in your synthesis, and report them as limitations;
8. **distinguish** keyword-based, semantic (AI) and citation-based search
   tools, and use AI at each stage without giving up reproducibility (see
   [Lecture 02](l_02_AITools.qmd)).

The running example is the literature on **capabilities and routines** — from
Nelson and Winter's evolutionary theory to dynamic capabilities in strategic
management. Shorter examples come from firm growth, evolutionary economic
geography, path dependence, and the debate on corporate social and financial
performance.

## 🧰 Tutorial and templates

- [**A mini systematic review in eight steps**](lit-review-tutorial/index.qmd) —
  the hands-on companion to the lecture. It walks you through a complete small
  review in Web of Science, from the concept table to the flow diagram, and
  includes an optional R part that builds on the implementation lab.
- The tutorial comes with three templates you can reuse for your term paper:
  a **search log**, a **screening sheet**, and a **concept matrix**.

Access to Web of Science is provided through the university library; see the
[ZHB database entry](https://dbis.ur.de/HDFL/resources/3366?lang=de).

## 📚 Mandatory Reading

- @snyder2019literature — a short overview of review types and how to choose
  between them, written for business research.
- @page2021prisma — the PRISMA 2020 statement. Concentrate on the checklist and
  the flow diagram; the rest you can skim.

## 🏆 Further Readings

*On method:*

- @tranfield2003towards — the classic argument for systematic reviews in
  management, and why they need to differ from the medical template.
- @webster2002analyzing — the origin of the concept matrix.
- @grant2009typology — fourteen review types, if you want the full map.
- @page2021prismaexplanation — the PRISMA explanation and elaboration paper;
  use it as a reference, not as reading.
- @rethlefsen2021prismas — PRISMA-S, on how to report the search itself.
- @gusenbauer2020which — which search systems are suitable for systematic
  reviews (and why Google Scholar is not one of them).
- The official [PRISMA website](https://www.prisma-statement.org/) with
  checklists and flow-diagram templates.

*Reviews used as examples in the lecture:*

- @becker2004organizational and @lane2006reification — two reviews that show
  how a concept drifts as a literature grows.
- @schilke2018quo — a content-analytic review of dynamic capabilities.
- @content2016related — a short review of 21 empirical studies in
  evolutionary economic geography.
- @aistleitner2021capability and @graebner2023degrowth — two systematic
  reviews I was involved in, discussed in the lecture as worked examples.

## ✍️ Exercises and coursework

*Take-home examination II (pass/fail; you must pass two of the three take-home
examinations to be admitted to the final exam — see the
[seminar description](/content/SeminarDescription.qmd)):*

- Conduct a small systematic literature review on a question that will be given
  to you. The task is published on
  [Moodle](https://elearning.uni-flensburg.de/moodle/course/view.php?id=17920)
  on 9 November 2026 and follows the steps of the
  [tutorial](lit-review-tutorial/index.qmd). Do not forget the
  [AI disclosure](ai-disclosure/index.qmd).

*Suggested exercise (not graded):*

- Take the literature review section of a paper you have recently read and fill
  in a concept matrix for the studies it cites. Is the section a synthesis, or a
  sequence of summaries?
